name: crypto-x25519
algorithm: std X25519 (RFC 7748) key exchange chained as RFC 7748 5.2's iteration: from k = 32 splitmix64 bytes and u = 9, n steps of pub = X25519(k, 9), acc ^= pub's low 8 bytes, (k, u) = (X25519(k, u), k); prints k's low 8 bytes xor acc (mk/crypto-x25519.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard X25519
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no X25519; no crate stands in

notes: Work per step: two X25519 ladders on every side, the public key of k and the shared secret of k and u. Mk crypto.X25519(k, 9) and crypto.X25519(k, u); Zig dh.X25519.recoverPublicKey(k) and dh.X25519.scalarmult(k, u); Go crypto/ecdh NewPrivateKey(k) (which runs the ladder on the base point: Go 1.27.3 crypto/ecdh/x25519.go) with PublicKey().Bytes(), then NewPublicKey(u) and ECDH. Go's std has no single-ladder X25519, so the row measures the exchange step on every side (CRY-1; the row before session 3 ran one ladder in Mk and Zig and two in Go). Ladders per second = 2 n / median.
The public key is folded into the checksum, so a column that skipped the base-point ladder would print another value.
Go: crypto/ecdh's field multiplication is assembly on amd64. Zig marks its field multiply callconv(bloaty_inline).
Checksums: recorded from `go run ./tools/bench verify` and `verify -publish-size` (status/std-crypto.md, session 3). Not published: no number here is a measurement.
